item-handbooktext-rift-sword-*: A sword assembled from a blade head and a handle. The blade decides its tier, metal, damage and most of its durability; the handle decides the grip and adds durability of its own. The two are independent, so any handle fits any blade.
item-handbooktext-handle: Cut a handle from a debarked log with a saw. Wrap it in cloth or leather to change its look, or fit a guard and bands to make a sturdier one. The metal of a fitted handle adds to the finished sword's durability.
item-handbooktext-blade-head: Smithed from an ingot. Its metal and tier set the sword's damage, mining tier and the bulk of its durability.
item-handbooktext-rift-shovel-*: A shovel assembled from a shovel head and two handles. The head decides its metal, digging speed and the bulk of its durability; the grip adds durability of its own. The shaft is always wood, whatever the handle is made of.
item-handbooktext-shovel-head: Smithed from an ingot, on the same pattern as a vanilla shovel head. Its metal sets the shovel's digging speed and most of its durability.
item-handbooktext-shovel-handle: A long shaft cut from a handle and a debarked log. It keeps whatever the handle carried - its grip, its wrap and its metal - so wrap a handle first and the shaft comes out wrapped.
